newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CHOICE SINKS AFTER POSTING HEFTY YEAR LOSS.
newsitem.headline: CHOICE SINKS AFTER POSTING HEFTY YEAR LOSS.

text.p: Shares in South African poultry and meat firm Choice Holdings Ltd sank on Thursday after the group posted a hefty year loss.
The firm saw earnings per share plummet to a loss of 338.2 cents, against 91.8 cents profit for the same period last time.

The firm had warned shareholders last month that its total attributable loss for the ear to February 28 would be greater than anticipated, but dealers said the market had still been surprised by the scale of the downturn.
"The numbers are not good at all," one dealer said.
Choice shares fell 20 cents to 170 cents, a dip of 10.5 percent that made it the fourth biggest early loser on the bourse.
Choice had a 102 million rand rights issue in December 1996 but said that in view of the continued losses further sources of fixed capital were now being sought.
Yabeng Investment Holding Co Ltd, which has a stake in the firm, had provided a further 40 million rand since the year-end, it added.
